units.text: INT. PYGMALION - CONTINUOUS

I want to be a lady in a flower shop stead of selling at the corner of Tottenham Court Road. But they won’t take me unless I can talk more genteel. He said he could teach me. Well, here I am ready to pay him—not asking any favor—and he treats me as if I was dirt.
units.name: THE FLOWER GIRL

units.text: How can you be such a foolish ignorant girl as to think you could afford to pay Mr. Higgins?
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Why shouldn’t I? I know what lessons cost as well as you do; and I’m ready to pay.
units.name: THE FLOWER GIRL

units.text: How much?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: THE FLOWER GIRL [coming back to him, triumphant] Now you’re talking!
I thought you’d come off it when you saw a chance of getting back a bit of what you chucked at me last night. [Confidentially] You’d had a drop in, hadn’t you?
HIGGINS [peremptorily] Sit down.
Oh, if you’re going to make a compliment of it—
units.name: THE FLOWER GIRL

units.text: HIGGINS [thundering at her] Sit down.
PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: severely.
Sit down, girl. Do as you’re told.
units.name: MRS

units.text: She places the stray chair near the hearthrug between Higgins and Pickering, and stands behind it waiting for the girl to sit down.
Ah—ah—ah—ow—ow—oo!
units.name: THE FLOWER GIRL

units.text: She stands, half rebellious, half bewildered.
PICKERING [very courteous] Won’t you sit down?
LIZA [coyly] Don’t mind if I do. [She sits down.
Pickering returns to the hearthrug].
What’s your name?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Liza Doolittle.
units.name: THE FLOWER GIRL

units.text: HIGGINS [declaiming gravely] Eliza, Elizabeth, Betsy and Bess, They went to the woods to get a bird’s nes’:
They found a nest with four eggs in it:
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: They took one apiece, and left three in it.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: They laugh heartily at their own wit.
Oh, don’t be silly.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: You mustn’t speak to the gentleman like that.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Well, why won’t he speak sensible to me?
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Come back to business. How much do you propose to pay me for the lessons?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Oh, I know what’s right. A lady friend of mine gets French lessons for eighteenpence an hour from a real French gentleman. Well, you wouldn’t have the face to ask me the same for teaching me my own language as you would for French; so I won’t give more than a shilling. Take it or leave it.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: HIGGINS [walking up and down the room, rattling his keys and his cash in his pockets] You know, Pickering, if you consider a shilling, not as a simple shilling, but as a percentage of this girl’s income, it works out as fully equivalent to sixty or seventy guineas from a millionaire.
How so?
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: Figure it out. A millionaire has about 150 pounds a day. She earns about half-a-crown.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: LIZA [haughtily] Who told you I only—
HIGGINS [continuing] She offers me two-fifths of her day’s income for a lesson.
Two-fifths of a millionaire’s income for a day would be somewhere about 60 pounds.
It’s handsome.
By George, it’s enormous! it’s the biggest offer I ever had.
LIZA [rising, terrified] Sixty pounds!
What are you talking about?
I never offered you sixty pounds.
Where would I get—
Hold your tongue.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: LIZA [weeping] But I ain’t got sixty pounds.
Oh—
Don’t cry, you silly girl. Sit down. Nobody is going to touch your money.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Somebody is going to touch you, with a broomstick, if you don’t stop snivelling. Sit down.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: LIZA [obeying slowly] Ah—ah—ah—ow—oo—o!
One would think you was my father.
If I decide to teach you, I’ll be worse than two fathers to you. Here
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: he offers her his silk handkerchief.
What’s this for?
units.name: LIZA

units.text: To wipe your eyes. To wipe any part of your face that feels moist. Remember: that’s your handkerchief; and that’s your sleeve. Don’t mistake the one for the other if you wish to become a lady in a shop.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Liza, utterly bewildered, stares helplessly at him.
It’s no use talking to her like that, Mr. Higgins: she doesn’t understand you. Besides, you’re quite wrong: she doesn’t do it that way at all
units.name: MRS. PEARCE
